message.content:
The drive from San Francisco to Los Angeles covers roughly **380–400 miles** (about 610–640 km) along I‑5 N/S. Under normal conditions—no major detours or heavy traffic—a typical trip takes around **6 hours**.  

Key points that can affect the actual duration:

| Factor | Typical Impact |
|--------|----------------|
| **Traffic** | Peak‑hour congestion on I‑5, especially near the Bay Area and the Los Angeles metro area, can add 30 minutes to an hour or more. |
| **Speed limits** | Most of I‑5 runs at 65–70 mph (105–112 km/h), but sections near cities drop to 55–60 mph (88–97 km/h). |
| **Stops** | A quick break for fuel, food, or restroom can add 15–20 minutes. |
| **Roadwork / Incidents** | Construction or accidents may cause detours that add 15–45 minutes depending on severity. |

So, if you leave during off‑peak times (mid‑morning or late evening) and avoid major construction zones, you’re looking at about **6 hours**. If you hit rush hour or encounter delays, plan for **7–8 hours** to stay comfortable.
